title: The Bridge of the Palatinate
premise: In 1747, in the Palatinate town of Falkenau, apprentice clockmaker Astrid Ravensworth arrives to repair the observatory's failing master clock just as winter floods close the great stone bridge — the only road out. Trapped, Astrid discovers the clock's mechanism has been deliberately sabotaged to mask a smuggling ledger implicating the Ravensworth family in a decades-old betrayal that cost a neighboring family their land and name. As the floodwaters rise and the magistrate demands a scapegoat, Astrid must repair the clock, expose the truth, and decide which family member takes the last berth on the ferry out — knowing the choice will either preserve the family or finally deliver justice. In the end, Astrid gives the berth to the wronged family's last surviving daughter, stays behind to face the consequences, and lets the repaired clock strike the hour that convicts their own blood.
about_author: Wendell Halloran is the pen name of a former horologist's apprentice who spent a decade restoring tower clocks across central Europe before turning to fiction. Their novels are known for meticulous period detail and protagonists caught between craft, conscience, and kin.

chapters.title: The Hour That Would Not Strike
chapters.summary: Astrid Ravensworth, POV. Summoned from Heidelberg to Falkenau, Astrid climbs the observatory tower and finds the master clock jammed by a filed gear tooth — deliberate work. The townsfolk watch coldly; someone whispers the name 'Ravensworth' with contempt. Emotional beat: unease beneath professional pride, the first hint that this repair is also an accusation.

chapters.title: Water at the Arches
chapters.summary: Astrid, POV. The river swells with autumn rain and the bridge closes for the season, stranding Astrid among strangers who resent them. Lodging with the ferryman's widow, Greta, Astrid learns the town still mourns the Albrecht family, dispossessed thirty years ago. Emotional beat: claustrophobia and the dawning sense of being a stranger in a story already underway.

chapters.title: A Ledger in the Case
chapters.summary: Astrid, POV. Cleaning the clock's case, Astrid finds a hidden compartment containing a ledger of tolls never paid — payments routed to a Ravensworth. Confronted, Uncle Konrad, the town's respected burgher who summoned Astrid, admits nothing but warns them to burn it. Emotional beat: loyalty cracking against evidence; the past stops being other people's.

chapters.title: The Albrecht Daughter
chapters.summary: Lena Albrecht, POV. Lena, a laundress living under a false name, recognizes the ledger as her family's stolen proof. She approaches Astrid not with anger but with a bargain: help her bring the truth before the spring assizes, and she'll testify the sabotage wasn't Astrid's doing. Emotional beat: wary alliance between two people the town has used differently.

chapters.title: What Konrad Buried
chapters.summary: Konrad, POV. Flashback chapters within his confession to his late wife's portrait: how he and Astrid's father falsified the tolls, ruined old Albrecht, and let the man die in debtor's prison. He believes silence kept the family alive. Emotional beat: guilt calcified into self-justification; the reader sees the crime whole.

chapters.title: The Magistrate's Question
chapters.summary: Astrid, POV. Magistrate Vogel, facing pressure over the sabotage, announces he'll charge whoever is found responsible — and hints that a foreign-born apprentice is convenient. Greta urges Astrid to finish repairs quietly and leave by ferry when the ice breaks. Emotional beat: fear sharpening into resolve; justice outside the law begins to look necessary because the law wants a shortcut.

chapters.title: Gears Against the Frost
chapters.summary: Astrid and Lena, alternating POV. Working nights, they rebuild the sabotaged escapement while copying the ledger for the assizes. Konrad discovers them; father-figure and apprentice face each other over the open clock case. He offers Astrid the family name, fully restored, if the ledger burns. Emotional beat: the temptation of belonging set against the cost of truth.

chapters.title: The Ice Breaks Early
chapters.summary: Astrid, POV. A thaw floods the valley weeks early; the ferry can make one crossing before the river becomes impassable, and there is exactly one berth left. Vogel moves to arrest Lena for the sabotage on planted evidence. Emotional beat: crisis compressing every theme — identity, loyalty, justice — into a single seat on a single boat.

chapters.title: The Last Berth
chapters.summary: Astrid, POV, climax. At the landing, Astrid puts Lena aboard with the ledger and stays, surrendering the escape Konrad arranged for them. As the master clock — repaired — strikes the hour, Astrid publicly reads the tolls aloud from the tower steps, naming their own family. Vogel must act; Konrad's silence finally costs him everything. Emotional beat: terrible clarity; the choice made without flinching.

chapters.title: What the Clock Keeps
chapters.summary: Astrid, POV, resolution. Spring assizes: Konrad confesses rather than let Astrid hang; the Albrecht lands are restored to Lena, who returns by the reopened bridge. Astrid, pardoned but no longer welcome as a Ravensworth, accepts the post of town clockkeeper. Final image: the master clock striking true, and Astrid finally at home inside history rather than beside it. Emotional beat: costly peace; identity rebuilt on truth instead of blood.
